newsitem.title: USA: Viacom to cut debt to $6-$8 bln in 2-3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Viacom to cut debt to $6-$8 bln in 2-3 yrs.

text.p: Viacom Chairman Sumner Redstone said Friday he expects to reduce the company's debt to $6-$8 billion over the next 24 to 36 months, from just under $10 billion now.
Redstone, speaking to Reuters following his presentation at a PaineWebber media conference in New York, emphasized the importance of debt reduction.
"We are not planning any major acquisitions of any kind whatsoever," he said.
The reduction in debt would come from expected increases in free cash flow as well as "discreet disposition of assets with no relation to core businesses," he said.
Redstone also said Viacom will decide which underperforming Blockbuster stores will be closed after the end of the current holiday sales season.
These closures, and the relocation of Blockbuster's headquarters to Dallas, may result in a charge against earnings, he said. He declined to elaborate.
On the overall performance of Blockbuster, which saw a turnaround in the third quarter, Redstone said, "I have every reason to expect the upward momentum will continue."

He said that within three to four years, Viacom's international revenues will grow to 70 percent of total revenues, up from 50 percent today, a shift driven partly by the appeal of such Paramount films as "Mission Impossible."
In the upcoming year Paramount is expected to release 16 to 18 new films, he said.
Viacom added that the Blockbuster stores that are under consideration for closure are some of the company's 500 Blockbuster music stores, not the video retailers.
